issues.body:
The runtime FROM moves from sha256:b0ae8e98...985 to sha256:fccdbb0a...96e, and the added comment lines push the FROM from line 76 to line 78. Three checked-in compliance records still cite the pre-PR values and are now false:

1. compliance/cis/evidence.md:33-36 (E-2, controls D-4.1/D-4.2/D-4.7) presents a literal command transcript:
     grep -nE '^FROM ' Dockerfile
     #  Dockerfile:76:  FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot@sha256:b0ae8e98...985
   Running that exact command against this PR head prints `78:` and `fccdbb0a`. An auditor reproducing the evidence gets a mismatch on both the line number and the digest, which is the precise failure mode this evidence file exists to prevent.

2. compliance/cis/controls.md:25 (D-4.1) and :26 (D-4.2) both cite `distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot@sha256:b0ae...` (`Dockerfile:76`).

3. compliance/slsa/evidence.md:115 (SL-B3-c) cites `FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot@sha256:b0ae8e98...` (runtime).

I confirmed these citations were ACCURATE before this PR (the FROM was at line 76 with the b0ae digest), so the drift is introduced here rather than pre-existing. Under the repo's honesty contract -- every claim traces to what the code actually does -- shipping a digest bump that silently invalidates its own compliance evidence is an incomplete change.

Separately and NOT attributable to this PR: compliance/cis/controls.md:25 also cites `Dockerfile:104` for the ENTRYPOINT, which is actually at line 125 (123 before this PR). That drift predates this change; flagging it only so it is not mistaken for collateral damage here.
issues.fix_hint:
Update the three citations in the same PR so the evidence stays reproducible:

- compliance/cis/evidence.md:35 -> `#  Dockerfile:78:  FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot@sha256:fccdbb0a...96e`
- compliance/cis/controls.md:25 and :26 -> `@sha256:fccd...` and `(Dockerfile:78)`
- compliance/slsa/evidence.md:115 -> `@sha256:fccdbb0a...`

Optionally also refresh the stale `Dockerfile:104` -> `Dockerfile:125` ENTRYPOINT reference in compliance/cis/controls.md:25 while in the file.

Longer term (out of scope for this PR -- file as a bead/issue rather than doing it here): these records embed a digest and a line number that must be hand-synced on every base bump. Either drop the line numbers and quote only the tag + digest, or add a doc-sync gate that greps the live Dockerfile and fails when a compliance citation no longer matches, so the next refresh cannot silently rot the evidence.
issues.title: Digest bump leaves three compliance evidence records quoting the OLD digest and the OLD FROM line number

issues.body:
Round 1 asked (minor) that the PR body record how the digest was resolved and that the nonroot variant/User were unchanged. The Dockerfile now carries the maintenance half of that -- "Refresh the digest when :nonroot advances with base-layer/security updates" -- which is accurate and is the right place for it.

I cannot confirm the PR-body half: `gh` is not available in this review environment, so I read only the diff and the checkout. Recording this as a nit rather than a repeat of the round-1 minor because I verified the underlying facts myself against the registry and they hold (tag is :nonroot, not :latest; User=65532 and Env unchanged; 17/18 layers identical). Nothing about the change is wrong -- only the audit trail may be thin.
issues.fix_hint: If not already there, add two lines to the PR body: the resolution command and its output (`crane digest gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot` -> sha256:fccdbb0a...96e), plus a note that User=65532, Env, and Entrypoint are unchanged versus the previous pin and that only the base OS layer moved. Non-blocking; fold it in alongside the compliance-doc fix.
issues.title: Round-1's provenance request is partially addressed in-file; the PR-body half is unverifiable from here

verdict.summary:
Round-1's major finding is genuinely FIXED. The comment no longer asserts a causal claim; it now states a standing property ("This is the multi-platform OCI index used by Buildx for the amd64 and arm64 release images"), which I verified is true and was true of the old pin too, so it no longer implies a single-arch bug was repaired. It is accurate against .github/workflows/release.yml:691 (platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64). The [GPT-5.6] marker matches repo convention (256 existing uses).

I re-verified the digest live against gcr.io: sha256:fccdbb0a...96e is exactly what the :nonroot tag resolves to today (NOT :latest, which is sha256:e8e7ee4b...), it is an application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json listing the same five platforms as the old pin (amd64, arm64/v8, arm/v7, s390x, ppc64le), and its amd64 config is byte-for-byte equivalent in posture: User=65532, same Env (PATH + SSL_CERT_FILE), no Entrypoint/Cmd. 17 of 18 layers are identical; only the bottom base-OS layer moved (875ea987 -> a5789fc4). So the bump itself is a clean, minimal, no-posture-change base refresh, and .trivyignore is CVE-id-keyed (not digest-coupled), so it is unaffected.

What blocks merge is COMPLETENESS, not the digest. This PR moves the digest and grows the runtime comment by two lines, which falsifies three auditor-facing compliance records that quote the old digest and the old FROM line number. compliance/cis/evidence.md:33-36 is presented as a literal transcript of `grep -nE '^FROM ' Dockerfile`; re-running it now prints Dockerfile:78 and fccdbb0a..., not Dockerfile:76 and b0ae8e98.... These citations were CORRECT before this PR, so this PR is what breaks them.

Progress note, stated plainly so it can be audited: I label this "improving" because the round-1 major was fixed exactly as hinted and round 2 introduced no new defect. The major below is pre-existing (it was equally true at round 1) and was missed by the prior round rather than caused by this round's edit.
